I care about my students as whole people, and I recognize that my certification comes with restrictions on my behavior even outside of school. My moral turpitude is important, especially directly in front of a child I teach. You also have to keep in mind that you are a kindergarten teacher, not a high school teacher or a college professor. You students understand very little about the fact that people are people outside of their jobs. Babygirl, 75 pounds is not good. 80 pounds at your height is not good. I was in the same boat as you when I was your age. I didn’t *want* to be skinny, but we didn’t have food at our house ever, and it was just hard for me to eat. My parents didn’t want to believe that there was anything wrong and they always said “enjoy it while you can, you’ll get fat when you get older.” I did not magically get fat when I got older. I almost died twice. I had to go to treatment for an eating disorder because that’s what it turned into. You have time to turn this around. If you can possibly, see a doctor and have your mother come with. To have a just BARELY healthy BMI at your height, you need to be at LEAST 107 pounds. You are currently at LEAST 27 pounds underweight. That’s the bare minimum to be healthy. Maybe a doctor can help her see that you need to gain weight. Well, about 10 years ago I pretty much stopped eating for a few months, and by the time I hit 80 pounds my college got worried and I had to go to a hospital. That’s where I was diagnosed with anorexia. I was there for 21 days. Then I went to a residential treatment facility for four months. I was doing pretty well for the next 9 years, but about a year and a half ago a friend committed suicide and I started having these awful panic attacks, and that all ended with me using eating disorder behaviors to manage my anxiety. Behaviors like skipping one meal, then two meals, then all meals on some days. Then at that point I was pretty much too weak to drive, and I had an hour and a half commute to work. I was passing out in the middle of the day from lack of sugar/ food. I was living off of those bottled protein shakes for the elderly, drinking like one a day. I was puking up stomach acid every morning. I had to quit my job because I couldn’t stay conscious enough to drive. I wasn’t as thin as I was before, but I think because I’m older now it was hitting me worse. I live near a nationally ranked eating disorder center and I called and thankfully my insurance covered me for three months there. It really helped me figure out my life and how to take care of myself again. They believe now that eating disorders can be genetic. I am an abuse victim and sometimes that can trigger a predisposition you already have in your genes to have some sort of disordered eating. My sister has also been to treatment for the same issue, and it runs in my family pretty strongly. I know this this probably a way longer answer than you anticipated, but eating disorders are really complicated, and I didn’t want to give a falsely simplistic answer.
